question: If $\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} A = \begin{bmatrix}-4 & 8 & 4 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 \\ -3 & 6 & 3\end{bmatrix}$, then the order of $A$ must be:
explanation:
Step 1 Determine the dimensions of the known matrices in the equation. The matrix on the left side is a column matrix with 3 rows and 1 column, so its order is $3 \times 1$. The resulting product matrix on the right has 3 rows and 3 columns, so its order is $3 \times 3$.

Step 2 Apply the fundamental rule of matrix multiplication. If a matrix of order $m \times n$ is multiplied by a matrix of order $p \times q$, the inner dimensions must match ($n = p$), and the resulting matrix will have the dimensions $m \times q$.

Step 3 Let the order of matrix $A$ be $p \times q$. From our knowns, a $(3 \times 1)$ matrix multiplied by a $(p \times q)$ matrix must produce a $(3 \times 3)$ matrix. Therefore, $p$ must be $1$, and $q$ must be $3$. The order of $A$ is $1 \times 3$.
